title: My kids and I made 3+ games this week
author: gadimus
selftext:
Here are two games I'd like to share. I'm sure no one wants to run random exe or osx applications from the internet but I'ma share them anyways.

There are fun little games made with Cursor and assets from [https://kenney.nl/](https://kenney.nl/) then free sfx sourced online - we used Suno for background music.

**Memo Racing (Made in <1 day)**

* Mario Kart-esque game with Kenney's race kit as the base game then cube animals swapped in and adjustments on camera angle, racing dynamics and of course 4-player split screen
* [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1fHQsHwuT4a4Y7QaeZiwCTTtAZGPh33Sn?usp=drive\_link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1fHQsHwuT4a4Y7QaeZiwCTTtAZGPh33Sn?usp=drive_link)

**Skelington Game (Made in 2 days)**

* Card Based Auto Battler Roguelike Army Builder Thing - Get Cards for your army, place them on the board, fight the other army, whoever does more damage wins
* [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1wXNqvIJLJIGJ4tfJbp8X13vqI3es5ePb?usp=drive\_link](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1wXNqvIJLJIGJ4tfJbp8X13vqI3es5ePb?usp=drive_link)

  
I've got a little 3d modelling experience from making 3d printable minifigs models in blender over the last few years so I was able to make some small tweaks. For the racing game I made a turtle character and the Skelington game I created a pack opening animation. Other than that these are all prompting based projects.

With any development project controlling scope is critical and I think vibe coding just takes that to the extreme. It's easy to have ideas but slapping them all together can create a knotted mess.

The biggest challenge I've found is balancing these games. The card battler is one that I'd love to add more cards to, more mechanics and features etc... etc... but things get out of control very very quickly and you can't just ask your agent to "balance it all" because while it can run simulations of battles it can't anticipate every broken combo that the user might come across - you maybe need to spend more than a day working on balance.

Overall super super fun projects. I love that this is doable now. Personally I have a weakness for shitty mobile clicker / rpg games. They scratch an itch but waste so much damn time and it's awesome to have an alternative. Making games scratches the same itch and it's so much more productive. Involving kids means you have testers that will find all the bugs AND you can create something together - it's awesome.
